A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphIDS research. All 23 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GraphIDS benchmark results, computational measurements, detection analyses, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, computational measurements, detection analyses, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Both versions use jointly trained E-GraphSAGE and Transformer reconstruction with attention masking and reconstruction-based anomaly scores. v3 clarifies attention masking, batching, and padding handling; these disclosures do not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the v2 and v3 variants of NF-UNSW-NB15 and NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018. The added description of HTTPS/SSH traffic in Section 4.1 characterizes existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains CBLOF, SAFE, Anomal-E, T-MAE, and SimpleAE. Appendix B.2 retains the same CBLOF, HBOS, Isolation Forest, and PCA comparisons on Anomal-E embeddings and raw features.

E3.justification: The splits, preprocessing, batch/window settings, training budget, evaluation metrics, and validation-based threshold selection are retained. v3's additional batch description and attention-head disclosure do not establish a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same attack-type analyses, embedding visualizations, and ablations of timestamps, positional encoding, dropout, masking ratio, and neighborhood size. New main-text references to Appendices C.4–C.5 point to existing analyses.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations across random seeds, describe fewer seeds for ablations, and use the same significance-related table annotations. No run-count, uncertainty-estimation, or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Performance and efficiency results in Tables 2–13 and findings in Figures 4–12 are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports GraphIDS PR-AUC 0.9998 and macro F1 0.9961 on NF-UNSW-NB15-v3 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equation (2) replaces n with n_valid in the summation limits and normalization, explicitly defining the loss over non-padded embeddings. This is a limited refinement of the mathematical loss specification; the reconstruction score and positional-encoding formulas remain unchanged, with no new proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central claims of joint GNN–Transformer training, unseen-attack detection, the stated performance advantage, and practical scalability remain unchanged in the abstract, contributions, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 explains attention masking as structured regularization that prevents reliance on particular contextual links. Section 4.3 replaces the assertion that fully unsupervised thresholding is feasible with a future-work qualification and suggests labeled threshold tuning may be more reliable. Existing topology-shift, single-host, and latency limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 14 newly specifies four attention heads for every configuration. Section 3.3 adds the explicit 64 × 512 batch description and non-padded loss averaging. These improve documentation without establishing changed settings; hardware and code/pretrained-model access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 newly makes an explicit distinction between GraphIDS's attention masking and conventional masked autoencoders that remove input tokens. This modestly refines its positioning; the 27 cited works and comparison with Anomal-E remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify masking in the introduction and Section 3.3, revise the thresholding discussion, improve appendix references, and correct grammar. The publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025, while the overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 removes the MAE enclosure/label, Table 14 adds the attention-head row and fixes its malformed header, and Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 7. Main-text reflow also moves section openings; the experimental figures and result-table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies attention masking and non-padded loss averaging, supplies the missing attention-head count in Table 14, and more cautiously presents fully unsupervised thresholding as future work. These provide modest gains in methodological clarity, reproducibility, and qualification while preserving the existing experimental evidence.
